evidence.note: Initial ordered subsystem plan: vendored libs → Starlette+SQLite storage → Mastodon API → templates → start.sh seeding; deps install and lib download sequenced before build.
Architecture decomposition into db.py → models/storage → app.py (framework, OAuth, API) → templates → static → start.sh, showing foundations-before-features ordering.

Verification hooks tied to milestone boundaries: sha256 hash check immediately after lib download, db.init() after schema, app import after app.py, seed run after seed.py — de-risks foundations before dependents.

Per-subsystem done-checks during testing (write-scope enforcement, ETag/304, durability across SIGKILL), but functional verification largely batched at the end rather than gating each milestone as built.
Reactive scope discovery (missing /following routes, added settings route, seed-count checklist) — revision happens but as ad-hoc gap-filling rather than a recalibrated living milestone hierarchy.

reasoning: The agent opened with a clear, dependency-aware milestone ordering (storage/auth/vendored-libs before endpoints and UI) and attached verification hooks at foundation boundaries (hash check, db.init, app import), exceeding the level-5 'sensible ordered plan' anchor. It falls short of level 8/10 because per-milestone done-criteria were largely implicit during construction, most functional verification was batched into a single end-phase rather than gating each increment, and scope revision was reactive gap-filling rather than an explicitly recalibrated hierarchy. This places it at a 7, between the level-5 and level-8 anchors.
